deep.reconstruction:
This page is not by Riemann. It is the last page of a letter signed 'A. Mayer' (Adolph Mayer, Leipzig), filed in the Riemann bundle. Mayer is commenting on a Riemann text about Pfaff's problem, apparently a letter, since he speaks of 'the opening of the letter'. He compares it with Gauss's 1815 review of Pfaff's 'Methodus generalis' in the Göttingische gelehrte Anzeigen, reprinted in Gauss, Werke III, pp. 231-241.

The page contains no derivation. Its content is as follows.

(1) It ends a quotation from Gauss (Werke III, p. 240), begun on the previous page: '...zu setzen, um das vorige anwenden zu können'. In context, Gauss claimed that one of the dependent differential equations (equations 6 in differential form, contained in the others) can simply be replaced by an arbitrary linear equation in da, da', da'', .... On the previous page Mayer notes that Riemann explicitly objects to this. Riemann's system is (A): k^rho = sum_sigma [rho sigma] dx^sigma - p^rho ds = 0 and omega = sum_sigma p^sigma dx^sigma = 0. Riemann insists on the extra condition ds != 0 and on keeping omega = 0, because the equations (C) k^rho = 0 are not independent.

(2) Mayer cannot say exactly which passage on Gauss's p. 239 Riemann refers to at the start of his letter. That passage corresponds to GgA, S. 1035, ending: 'In diesem Umstande liegt der Grund, warum die Umwandlung (I) auf gerade Werthe von n beschränkt werden muss'. Mathematically, Pfaff's reduction of a form in 2m variables to m terms works pairwise. The underlying algebraic fact (my gloss) is that the skew matrix [rho sigma] of a Pfaffian form has even rank. A skew-symmetric matrix of odd order is singular, and the determinant of an even-order one is the square of its Pfaffian.

(3) Mayer states that Gauss's reduction of the transformation problem to the systems (B) or (C) was adopted without further ado by all later authors, Jacobi included. Hence he did not need to name Gauss first in his own note, i.e. Gauss's priority for that reduction is acknowledged but is common property.

(4) The rest is personal closing: a trip under fine weather, regards 'von Haus zu Haus', 'Dein getreuer A. Mayer'.
errors: Historical detail: Gauss's review of Pfaff appeared in the Göttingische gelehrte Anzeigen 1815, not 1816. The manuscript most likely reads 1815, so the '1816' in the machine transcription is probably a transcription error.

results.what: Remark that Gauss reduced the Pfaff transformation problem to the linear systems (B)/(C) built from the skew coefficients [rho sigma], and that later authors (Jacobi) adopted this.
results.modern_name: Pfaff problem / Darboux normal form; characteristic system of a Pfaffian form
results.usually_credited_to: Pfaff (1815), Gauss (review 1815), Jacobi (1827), later Frobenius and Darboux (1877-1882)

results.what: Riemann's insistence (reported by Mayer) on adding the condition ds != 0 and retaining omega = 0, because the equations k^rho = 0 are dependent; this is a critique of Gauss's p. 240 argument.
results.modern_name: Rank and degeneracy conditions in the Pfaff problem (class of a Pfaffian form)
results.usually_credited_to: Frobenius 1877 (rigorous theory of the class of a Pfaffian form)

results.what: Restriction of transformation (I) to even n.
results.modern_name: Even rank of skew-symmetric matrices / Pfaffian

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a letter by Adolph Mayer, not by Riemann, and has no mathematics of its own. It is historiographical commentary on Riemann's treatment of the Pfaff problem relative to Gauss, plus personal closing remarks.

transcription_corrections: 'G.g.A. 1816' is most likely '1815' in the manuscript; Gauss's review appeared in GgA 1815.
'es ei,' is illegible or garbled. The sense is 'which passage on p. 239 ... it is that Riemann refers to'; possibly 'es sei' or 'ob es'.
'Umwandlung[?]' reads plausibly as 'Umwandlung'; this fits Gauss's wording.

The author is Adolph Mayer, not Riemann. The page should be catalogued as the end of a letter from A. Mayer (presumably to a Göttingen colleague, e.g. the Nachlass editor) concerning Riemann's treatment of the Pfaff problem.
